scope: Controlled synthetic Stage 16 smoke run for ARC concept transfer.
note: Tiny CPU run over prepared synthetic Hotpot-style rows. This validates the routing hook and gives an early transfer signal; it is not a full benchmark.

dataset.design: Rows include distant support windows and answer windows that are not always identical to support windows.

interpretation: relative_support transferred the relativeness/counting idea into an existing AOB routing mechanism.
It preserved support-window hit rate at 1.0 while improving answer-window hit rate over oracle_support from 0.6667 to 1.0 on this controlled split.
It matched oracle_support final F1 in this tiny run and beat learned_distinct final F1, but this is too small to claim general improvement.
The large oracle_support loss is expected in cases where support-only routing omits the answer window; relative_support includes answer as a role and avoids that failure mode.
Next empirical step is a real Stage 16 screen with relative_support included, ideally across seeds and without relying on answer-window oracle labels at test time.
